cashflow.title: Compare retirement versus college funding amounts
cashflow.why: The plan says retirement saving and college funding compete for the same cash while you run a yearly shortfall.
steps: List monthly cash available after taxes and spending
Write target monthly amounts for retirement and college
Adjust until monthly totals fit your current shortfall

cushion.title: Set aside near‑term cash for goals
cushion.why: The plan notes you’ve already earmarked a $6,000 vacation and Ethan’s $12,500 college payment, leaving a small extra cushion.
steps: Move $6,000 into a separate vacation savings account
Move $12,500 into a separate short‑term college savings account
Keep those accounts separate from your emergency reserve

retirement.title: Confirm whether a workplace retirement plan exists
retirement.why: The plan says knowing if a workplace retirement plan is available will shape your retirement saving options.
steps: Email or call your HR or payroll contact this month
Ask whether a 401(k) or similar plan is offered
Note plan start dates, employer match, and contribution limits

college.title: Decide how to fund Ethan’s near‑term college cost
college.why: The plan flags Ethan’s upcoming college payments competing with retirement and notes you have $0 in 529s.
steps: Confirm the exact amount and due date for Ethan’s payment
Choose source: cash on hand, taxable savings, or other
Record that funding choice in your monthly cash plan
